primitives.name: Schema-Only LLM SQL Generation
primitives.verbatim_quote: (b) Schema-only LLM SQL generation: the LLM sees the schema (not the data) and emits SQL; executed against MariaDB.
primitives.assumptions: LLM operates on schema alone; SQL output is executable against database.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Query resolution fails if schema misaligned with data.

layer2.mapping: LLM-generated SQL maps to GSE's nflverse/odds schema via deterministic query translation.
layer2.telemetry: Query execution success rate and SQL validity check.

primitives.name: Just-In-Time Materialized Views
primitives.verbatim_quote: (c) Just-in-time views: expensive temporal aggregations (per-gameweek history, future fixtures) materialized as in-memory tables on demand, then queried.
primitives.assumptions: Temporal queries are expensive; pre-materialization improves latency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance degrades without sufficient memory or caching.

layer2.mapping: Temporal aggregations in GSE are cached as in-memory views for low-latency access during live query processing.
layer2.telemetry: View creation time and query response latency.

primitives.name: Entity Resolution
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model (a) Entity resolution: map team/player mentions in the question to DB ids before SQL generation.
primitives.assumptions: Natural language contains named entities that map to database identifiers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Resolution fails if ambiguous or missing entity mappings exist.

layer2.mapping: Named entities in NL queries resolve to NFLverse IDs via GSI's entity linking module.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of entity-to-ID mapping and false positive rate.

These components form a robust pipeline where each step is deterministic and verifiable. The failure mode occurs when LLM hallucinates SQL, views are stale, or entity resolution mismatches. The system's strength lies in its compositional modularity and verification gates—scalar answers are checked for exact match, while tabular results use a correctness protocol. This aligns with GSE’s need for deterministic, fast, and safe query execution over live NFL data.
